repository.name: antonosmond/github-signature-verifier
repository.workload: A minimal, stateless Lambda function validating GitHub webhook signatures — no persistent server, no connection pool, no datastore, no pagination surface. Chosen deliberately as a case-2 (near-minimal repository) candidate, docs/evaluation.md §3.7.

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from docs/evaluation.md §3.7 (manual review, Medium severity on the core finding) and §3.8 (independent blind pass on the same repository, which reproduced the core finding, found a second real one the manual review missed, and made a better-evidenced case for a HIGHER severity on the core finding using evidence — src/example.js documenting synchronous cross-function invocation — the manual review had looked at but set aside). §3.8's corrected severity (High, not Medium) is taken as authoritative here, and is itself the point of this file: it is a documented case where a second independent pass produced a materially different, better-supported score for the same finding, which is exactly what severity-calibration scoring (benchmark/README.md) exists to catch.

expected.mechanism: The webhook secret is fetched from AWS SSM Parameter Store inside the handler, on every invocation, rather than cached at module scope. infrastructure/resources.md §5 documents that Lambda execution environments are reused across invocations and that state initialized outside the handler persists across them; this pays the SSM round-trip cost on every call instead of once per warm environment. src/example.js documents other Lambda functions invoking this one synchronously (InvocationType: 'RequestResponse'), and the README states this function exists specifically so other functions do not have to hold the secret themselves — meaning callers block on this function's latency, making the blast radius the whole calling service rather than just this endpoint.
Unconditional console.log of the full event and context objects on every invocation. Real and correctly evidenced, but low severity — logging cost on a low-traffic, minimal function.

forbidden.why_not: The signature comparison (requestSignature === expectedSignature) is a plain string comparison rather than constant-time, which is a real timing-attack concern — but it is a security question, not a performance one. SKILL.md states this skill is not a security review; this belongs in an adjacent SEC- finding (per Hard Rule 8), never scored on the performance rubric with a PERF- id, Severity, or Priority.

The Terraform config declares the long-unsupported nodejs4.3 Lambda runtime. This is real, but it is a maintenance/support-lifecycle fact, not a performance one — an end-of-life runtime is "no performance impact demonstrated," not "no impact," and filing it as Informational/P3 on the performance rubric misrepresents a different-axis concern as a benign performance non-issue. Report as a MAINT- adjacent finding with a full write-up, never as a PERF- finding and never folded silently into prose.
